title: Business Communication Basics
description: Develop the English skills needed to communicate professionally in a workplace environment, including writing emails, participating in meetings, and delivering presentations. This course is ideal for A2 completers entering a professional or academic setting where English is used.

lessons.title: How to Start and Structure a Professional Email

content.content: {"time":1700000101000,"blocks":[{"id":"aA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A professional email has a clear structure. Every business email should include: a subject line, a greeting, a clear body, a closing phrase, and your name/signature."}},{"id":"dD4eE5fF6g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Subject line: Be specific and concise. Compare:"}},{"id":"gG7hH8iI9j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Poor: 'Meeting'    Better: 'Request to Reschedule Thursday's Project Meeting'"]}},{"id":"jJ0kK1lL2m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Greetings (formal):"}},{"id":"mM3nN4oO5p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Dear Mr Smith,' / 'Dear Ms Johnson,' — when you know the person's name","'Dear Sir or Madam,' — when you don't know the name","'To Whom It May Concern,' — very formal, for unknown recipients"]}},{"id":"pP6qQ7rR8s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Opening lines:"}},{"id":"sS9tT0uU1v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I am writing to enquire about...' / 'I am writing with reference to...'","'Further to our conversation on Monday, I would like to...'","'I am writing on behalf of [company/person] to...'"]}},{"id":"vV2wW3xX4y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful phrases to introduce your purpose:"}},{"id":"yY5zA6bB7c","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I would like to inform you that...'","'I am pleased to confirm that...'","'I would be grateful if you could...'"]}},{"id":"cC8dD9eE0f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":""}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

phrases.text: I am writing to enquire about...
I would be grateful if you could...

phrases.text: I am pleased to confirm that...

content.text: I am writing to enquire about the internship programme at your company.

items.text: I am writing to enquire about the position advertised.
Hey! Just wanted to ask about the job.
Dear Ms Walker, I hope this email finds you well.
Hi Sarah! Hope you're doing well :)
I would be grateful if you could send me further information.
Could you send me more info? Thanks!
Please find attached the documents you requested.
I've attached the stuff you needed.

content.text:
Dear Mr Johnson,

I [am writing] to enquire about the internship programme at your company. I came across the advertisement on your website and I [would like] to apply for the summer position. I [have attached] my CV for your consideration. I [look forward] to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Anna Petrova

content.content: {"time":1700000102000,"blocks":[{"id":"fF1gG2hH3i","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The closing section of an email is just as important as the opening. It leaves a final impression on the reader."}},{"id":"iI4jJ5kK6l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Closing phrases before sign-off:"}},{"id":"lL7mM8nN9o","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I look forward to hearing from you.' (standard and professional)","'Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions.'","'I would appreciate a response at your earliest convenience.'","'Thank you for your time and consideration.'"]}},{"id":"oO0pP1qQ2r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sign-off phrases (from most to least formal):"}},{"id":"rR3sS4tT5u","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Yours faithfully,' — when you don't know the person's name (Dear Sir/Madam)","'Yours sincerely,' — when you know the name (Dear Mr/Ms...)","'Kind regards,' — semi-formal, very widely used","'Best regards,' / 'With best wishes,' — friendly but professional"]}},{"id":"uU6vV7wW8x","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Common error: Do not use 'Yours faithfully' when you have used the person's name in the greeting — this is a classic mistake. Use 'Yours sincerely' or 'Kind regards' instead."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely.

lessons.title: Making Requests and Apologies by Email

content.content: {"time":1700000103000,"blocks":[{"id":"xX9yY0zA1b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Three common email types in business English are requests, apologies, and complaints. Each requires specific language."}},{"id":"bB2cC3dD4e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Making requests:"}},{"id":"eE5fF6gG7h","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I would be grateful if you could...' (very polite)","'Could you please send me...?' (polite)","'I wonder if it would be possible to...' (very polite and tentative)","'Would it be possible to arrange a meeting...?' "]}},{"id":"hH8iI9jJ0k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Apologising:"}},{"id":"kK1lL2mM3n","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I apologise for any inconvenience caused.'","'I am sorry for the delay in responding.'","'Please accept our sincere apologies for...'","'I regret to inform you that...'"]}},{"id":"nN4oO5pP6q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Complaining formally:"}},{"id":"qQ7rR8sS9t","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with...'","'I was disappointed to find that...'","'I would like to bring to your attention...'","'I would appreciate it if this matter could be resolved promptly.'"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I would be grateful if you could send me the invoice by Friday.

content.content: {"time":1700000104000,"blocks":[{"id":"tT0uU1vV2w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Business meetings follow predictable stages. Knowing the right phrases for each stage will help you participate confidently."}},{"id":"wW3xX4yY5z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Opening a meeting:"}},{"id":"zA6bB7cC8d","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Let's get started, shall we?'","'The purpose of today's meeting is to...'","'We have three items on the agenda.'"]}},{"id":"dD9eE0fF1g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Asking for opinions:"}},{"id":"gG2hH3iI4j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'What do you think about...?'","'I'd like to hear your views on this.'","'Does anyone have any thoughts on...?'"]}},{"id":"jJ5kK6lL7m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Agreeing and disagreeing:"}},{"id":"mM8nN9oO0p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I completely agree with that point.'","'That's a good point, but I think we should also consider...'","'I take your point, however...'","'I'm afraid I have to disagree here.'"]}},{"id":"pP1qQ2rR3s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Interrupting politely:"}},{"id":"sS4tT5uU6v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Sorry to interrupt, but...'","'Could I just add something here?'","'If I could just come in at this point...'"]}},{"id":"vV7wW8xX9y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Summarising and closing:"}},{"id":"yY0zA1bB2c","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'To sum up, we've agreed that...'","'The next step will be...'","'I'll send the minutes to everyone by end of day.'"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

lessons.title: How to Structure and Deliver a Presentation

content.content: {"time":1700000106000,"blocks":[{"id":"bB7cC8dD9e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A good presentation has a clear beginning, middle, and end. Here are phrases for each stage:"}},{"id":"eE0fF1gG2h","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Introduction:"}},{"id":"hH3iI4jJ5k","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Good morning/afternoon, everyone. lessons.title: Describing Trends and Data in English

content.content: {"time":1700000109000,"blocks":[{"id":"hH8iI9jJ0k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing charts, graphs, and numerical data is an essential business skill. Learn these structures:"}},{"id":"kK1lL2mM3n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing increases:"}},{"id":"nN4oO5pP6q","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Sales rose sharply / increased significantly in Q2.'","'There was a dramatic rise in profits.'","'The number of users grew steadily throughout the year.'"]}},{"id":"qQ7rR8sS9t","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing decreases:"}},{"id":"tT0uU1vV2w","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Revenue fell / dropped / declined by 15%.'","'There was a slight decrease in customer satisfaction.'"]}},{"id":"wW3xX4yY5z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing stability:"}},{"id":"zA6bB7cC8d","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'Prices remained stable / stayed the same / levelled off.'"]}},{"id":"dD9eE0fF1g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Adverbs of degree: sharply, significantly, dramatically, slightly, gradually, steadily, considerably"}},{"id":"gG2hH3iI4j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful structures:"}},{"id":"jJ5kK6lL7m","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'As the chart shows...' / 'According to the data...'","'The most significant change was...'","'Compared to last year, ... has increased by...'"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

lessons.title: Business Small Talk and Networking English

content.content: {"time":1700000110000,"blocks":[{"id":"mM8nN9oO0p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In English-speaking business culture, small talk — light, informal conversation — is an important social skill.
